purpose: Prove whether the first operational capability slices from PRs #75-#93 already exist on canonical main before copying or recreating them.

semantic_result.reason: Stable main already has strong OMS/order-mutation durability, but it has no durable Bybit Demo single-writer lease, active-excursion checkpoint, or append-only approval/protected-entry/terminal-evidence stores. These are different operational control-state contracts and must not be faked by relabeling generic OMS tables.

extraction_decision.implementation_rule: Extract only the final v119/v120 durable operational state semantics and tests needed by later current controls; reuse canonical main OMS/persistence conventions where compatible and do not introduce later ARM, broker client, strategy, or order-write composition in C2A.

c2a_acceptance_contract: v119 singleton runtime lease is durable and has no TTL or automatic stale takeover
v119 active excursion checkpoint uses deterministic CAS/revision semantics
v120 approval authorization is append-only and has no order-submit capability
v120 protected-entry provenance is append-only and has no order-submit capability
v120 terminal evidence is append-only and diagnostics-only
database-level immutability/privilege controls are qualified on PostgreSQL 16
no Bybit network call is required by the C2A qualification
